We need propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: step1: sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So forward: sulfonyl chloride + amine -> sulfonamide. Retrosynthetic: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride and amine.

Our target has sulfonamide linking a phenyl sulfonyl to an aniline (the first phenyl with methyl). So disconnection: break S-N to give sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) and aniline (the phenyl with methyl attached to N). The sulfonyl chloride would be: p-methyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) with sulfonyl attached to that ring. The sulfonyl group attached to that ring is attached to the aniline (the first phenyl). So sulfonyl chloride precursor: p-methyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonyl is attached to the first phenyl (with methyl) via N. The sulfonyl group is attached to second phenyl ring (c2ccc...). The sulfonyl group is attached to that second phenyl ring (as sulfonyl attached to that ring). The N of sulfonamide is attached to first phenyl (with methyl). So sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the second phenyl ring bearing sulfonyl chloride (SO2Cl) attached to that ring. So structure: c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2 (para? Actually the sulfonyl attached to that ring at position where N attaches). So we need that.

Second step: amide formation between the α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (C= C C(=O)N...) and an aniline (c3ccccc3N). The forward: carboxylic acid + amine -> amide via coupling. Retrosynthetic: break C-N amide bond to give carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The acid is: trans-3-(phenylamino)acrylic acid? Actually the fragment: /C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N . So the acid is trans-3-(phenylamino)acrylic acid? Wait the amide is C(=O)N attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N). So the acid precursor is the α,β-unsaturated acid: C= C C(=O)OH (cinnamic acid). Actually the amide carbonyl attached to phenyl amine, so the acid is trans-3-phenylamido? No the amide is formed from acid and aniline, so acid is C= C C(=O)OH (cinnamic acid). The amide product attaches the aniline to carbonyl. So retrosynthesis: break amide to give cinnamic acid and aniline.

Third step: Doebner modification to form the α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde (benzaldehyde) and malonic acid. So forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid). So retrosynthetic: break C=C double bond to give benzaldehyde and malonic acid.

Thus three steps: 1) sulfonamide formation, 2) amide coupling, 3) Doebner modification.

We need template IDs for each step. We need to search for templates matching these transformations.

First, sulfonamide formation: functional_groups_formed: sulfonamides, bonds_formed: S-N. Use search with functional_groups_formed ["sulfonamides"] and maybe bonds_formed? But bond format requires "6-6". Not needed. Let's search with functional_groups_formed only.
